_comment: All original Moodshop writing. No quotes from anyone else, no AI call at runtime, nothing generated on a server. The tools shuffle and compose these blocks client-side, which is why they work offline and instantly.

calm: Nothing is asking anything of you for the length of this sentence.
Your shoulders have been climbing toward your ears since this morning. You're allowed to let them down.
The list is still there. It has been patient this long; it can be patient another minute.
You don't have to arrive anywhere. You're already here, which was the only requirement.
Still water isn't doing anything impressive. That's the point of it.
Slow is not the same as late.
You can put it down without putting it away.
peace: It's quiet, and for once that isn't the sound of something about to go wrong.
You spent so long braced that unclenching feels like a skill you have to relearn.
You're allowed to stop checking whether you're okay. You can just be okay.
This didn't get fixed. You got bigger around it. That counts.
There is nothing you need to do with a good hour except be in it.
Peace usually arrives without an announcement, which is why people miss it.
nostalgia: You don't miss the place. You miss who you got to be there.
Some memories hurt because they were beautiful, and that's the whole reason.
There's a version of you still standing in that light, and you can't write to them.
The song didn't change. You did, and now it means something else.
You remember the exact pitch of a voice calling your name from another room.
Ordinary days become the ones you'd pay to return to. Nobody tells you which ones at the time.
It wasn't better. It was just yours.
love: They keep turning up in your ordinary hours, uninvited, welcome.
You've drafted it a hundred times and sent none of them.
Love is mostly noticing. The grand parts are rare and the noticing is daily.
You want them to be okay even in the version of the story where they aren't yours.
Some people never leave your life. They just stop being in the room.
It's not that you can't stop thinking about them. It's that you've stopped wanting to.
Saying it out loud costs something. Not saying it costs more, later.
joy: You are allowed to feel good for no reason. There's no permission slip.
Happiness doesn't have to be earned back like a debt.
You laughed today and didn't check first whether you were allowed.
Not everything good is the beginning of something you'll lose.
Let it be small. Small is what most of it is made of.
The lightness was always yours. You just put it somewhere and forgot.
You don't owe anyone an explanation for a good hour.
hope: The change starts before there's any proof of it. That's how mornings work.
You can't see the light yet because it hasn't reached the part of the sky you're facing.
Nothing you can point to has shifted. That isn't the same as nothing shifting.
You've survived every day that you were sure you wouldn't. The record is perfect.
Not optimism. Just the refusal to call it final while it's still moving.
Something is going to happen that you haven't thought of yet.
It doesn't have to get better today. It only has to not be finished.
hurt: It isn't the moment that keeps stinging. It's what the moment revealed.
You found out how much room you took up in their decisions. Not much, it turned out.
You're not too sensitive. You were paying attention.
The apology you're waiting for may not be coming, and you're allowed to stop waiting anyway.
Trust wasn't built for what they did with it.
You keep explaining it to them in your head because they never let you finish out loud.
You can forgive someone and still not want them back.
sorrow: Nobody is going to rush you toward the door marked fine.
Some things don't resolve. They just get carried differently over time.
It's heavy today. That's information, not a failure.
You don't need a reason that's big enough. It's already heavy without one.
Not every hard day is the start of a hard year.
You carried it and nobody watched you do it. It still counts.
You're allowed to be in the part where it hurts, for as long as that part lasts.
grief: The habits haven't caught up yet. That isn't a failure to move on.
That's just what love does when it loses its address.
You still set the table for one more sometimes, before you remember.
A stranger's laugh. A coat like theirs. It never gives warning.
They were here. Being gone doesn't erase having been here.
Nobody can tell you how long this should take, and anyone who tries is wrong.
You're allowed to laugh today. It isn't a betrayal of anything.
rage: You've been so reasonable, for so long, to people who never returned the favour.
You are not too much for being furious about this. You are correctly sized.
There was never going to be a right moment. That's how they kept it.
Calm isn't always the goal. Sometimes it's just the thing that's expected of you.
You swallowed the sharp thing again. It's still in there.
Being angry about it is not the same as being ruled by it.
You're allowed to stop explaining yourself to someone who was never listening.
loneliness: You can be in a room full of people and not be with any of them.
Nobody checks on the person everyone checks in with.
It isn't about how many people are nearby. It's about being seen by them.
You'd have to explain too much, so you say you're fine, so nobody learns otherwise.
Being alone and being lonely happen to use the same room.
Someone would come if you asked. The hard part has always been asking.
This isn't proof that you're unlovable. It's proof that it's late.
anxiety: Your head has run the same three minutes forty times. It isn't solving them.
The loop is loud, and loud has convinced you it's useful.
You're rehearsing a conversation that may never happen, for an audience of one.
Most of what you're bracing for does not arrive.
You can't think your way out of a body that's still running.
It's worse at night because there's nothing else in the room. That's all that's changed.
You are not behind. You're just awake at the wrong hour for perspective.

messages._comment: Composed, not generated: opening (by who it's for) + body (by what you want to say, in the tone you pick) + closing (by tone). 7x2 openings, 8x6 bodies, 6x2 closings compose 336 distinct messages, all hand-written.

recipients.label: Someone I love
openings: I've started this more times than I'll admit.
There's something I keep not saying to you.

recipients.label: Someone I miss
openings: You've been on my mind, which you probably already guessed.
It's been a while, and you still come up.

recipients.label: Someone who hurt me
openings: I've had this conversation with you in my head enough times to write it down.
I'm not writing this to start anything.

recipients.label: Someone I hurt
openings: I'm not going to explain it away.
You don't owe me a reply to this.

recipients.label: Someone I want to thank
openings: I don't think you know what you did.
This is overdue and I'd rather send it late than not at all.

recipients.label: Someone I need to say goodbye to
openings: I've been putting this off because writing it makes it real.
This is the last thing I want to say, and I want to say it properly.

recipients.label: Myself
openings: You've been carrying this for a while now.
Nobody else is going to say this to you, so here it is.

miss.simple: I miss you. That's the whole message.
miss.warm: I miss you — not dramatically, just steadily, the way you notice a room is colder than it used to be.
miss.emotional: I miss you in the ordinary parts of the day, which is the part nobody warns you about. Not the anniversaries. Tuesdays.
miss.romantic: I miss you the way you miss a season. Everything still works without it; it's just less warm.
miss.honest: I miss you, and I've been pretending that's a smaller thing than it is.
miss.closure: I miss you, and I've decided that missing you doesn't have to mean waiting for you.

sorry.simple: I'm sorry. I'm not going to dress it up.
sorry.warm: I'm sorry. I've thought about it properly, and you were right to feel the way you did.
sorry.emotional: I'm sorry. I keep replaying the moment I could have chosen differently, and I keep watching myself not do it.
sorry.romantic: I'm sorry. Of everything I've been careless with, you're the one I'd most like back.
sorry.honest: I'm sorry. Not sorry-you-felt-that-way — sorry I did it, and sorry it took me this long to say so.
sorry.closure: I'm sorry. I'm not asking you to do anything with that. I just needed it to have been said.

love.simple: I love you. I should say it more often than I do.
love.warm: I love you — the everyday kind, the kind that shows up in what I notice about you.
love.emotional: I love you, and it startles me sometimes how much of my ordinary life has you in it.
love.romantic: I love you. You turn up in my quietest hours and make them worth having.
love.honest: I love you, and saying it out loud costs me something, which is probably how I know it's true.
love.closure: I love you. I'm telling you because not telling you was becoming the heavier thing to carry.

thanks.simple: Thank you. You probably don't know how much it mattered.
thanks.warm: Thank you. You did something small and it held me up longer than you'd guess.
thanks.emotional: Thank you. There was a stretch where I wasn't doing well, and you were kind without making a thing of it, and I've never forgotten.
thanks.romantic: Thank you for the version of me I got to be around you. I liked him better.
thanks.honest: Thank you. I'm bad at saying this, which is why it's arriving in writing and late.
thanks.closure: Thank you. Whatever else this was, that part was real and I'm not taking it back.

forgive.simple: I forgive you. I'd rather put it down than keep holding it.
forgive.warm: I forgive you. It took a while, and I'd rather tell you than let you assume.
forgive.emotional: I forgive you. Not because it didn't hurt — it did, more than I let on — but because carrying it has stopped doing anything for me.
forgive.romantic: I forgive you. What we had deserves to be remembered as more than how it ended.
forgive.honest: I forgive you, and I'm still allowed to not want things back the way they were.
forgive.closure: I forgive you. That's the end of it for me, and I'm saying so out loud so it stays ended.

closure.simple: I think I need to stop waiting for this to make sense.
closure.warm: I'd like to close this gently, if we can. No hard feelings, just an ending.
closure.emotional: I've been waiting for an explanation that I don't think is coming, and the waiting has cost me more than the answer would be worth.
closure.romantic: I'd rather remember this well than keep it open badly.
closure.honest: I need this to be finished. Not because I stopped caring — because leaving it open is doing me harm.
closure.closure: I'm closing this. Not angrily. I just don't want to keep living in a room with no door.

think.simple: I still think about you. That's all.
think.warm: I still think about you, and it's usually a good thought, in case you were wondering.
think.emotional: I still think about you at the strangest times — a street, a song, a certain kind of afternoon light — and it never gives me any warning.
think.romantic: You left my life and somehow never left my thoughts.
think.honest: I still think about you. I'm not sure what you're supposed to do with that, and I wanted to say it anyway.
think.closure: I still think about you, less often now, and more kindly. I think that's how this is supposed to go.

bye.warm: Goodbye. I hope the next part is good to you.
bye.emotional: Goodbye. I keep looking for a bigger word and there isn't one — everything I'd add would just be me stalling.
bye.romantic: Goodbye. You were one of the good parts, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise to make this easier.
bye.honest: Goodbye. I'm not slamming anything shut. I'm just done standing in the doorway.
bye.closure: Goodbye. Genuinely, and for good, and without any of it having been wasted.

warm: Take care of yourself — I mean that plainly.
emotional: I don't need a reply. I needed it to exist somewhere outside my own head.
You can do whatever you like with this. I just couldn't keep holding it.
romantic: Whatever happens next, I'm glad it was you.
I'd choose it again, knowing the ending.
honest: I'm not expecting anything back from this.
That's the true version, which is the only one worth sending.
closure: I'm not looking for a response. This one is for me.
That's the last of it, and it's a relief to have put it down.

lines.short: You're on my mind. That's all.
lines.sweet: You turn up in my ordinary hours and make them better.
lines.emotional: I don't always know how to say it out loud, so I'm sending it instead.
lines.deep: Some people never really leave your life. They just stop being in the room.

lines.sweet: It's been a while, and you still come up.
lines.emotional: I miss you on Tuesdays, which is the part nobody warns you about.
lines.deep: I don't miss the place. I miss who I got to be there, with you in it.

lines.sweet: You did something small once and it held me up longer than you'd guess.
lines.emotional: There was a stretch where I wasn't doing well, and you were kind without making a thing of it.
lines.deep: Thank you for the version of me I got to be around you.

lines.sweet: I've thought about it properly, and you were right to feel how you felt.
lines.emotional: I keep replaying the moment I could have chosen differently, and watching myself not do it.
lines.deep: I'm not asking you to do anything with this. I just needed it to have been said.

lines.short: You've got this. I'm not just saying it.
lines.sweet: Whatever tomorrow is, I think you'll be alright in it.
lines.emotional: You've survived every day you were sure you wouldn't. The record is perfect.
lines.deep: The change starts before there's any proof of it. I can see it even if you can't yet.

lines.sweet: I hope the next part of it is good to you.
lines.emotional: I keep looking for a bigger word than goodbye and there isn't one.
lines.deep: You were here. Being gone doesn't erase having been here.

prompts2am.text: What would you say if there were no consequences?
What are you pretending doesn't bother you?
What are you hoping tomorrow feels like?
What would you tell your younger self?
What have you not said out loud to anyone?
Which conversation are you still having in your head?
What are you afraid is true?
Who would you call if it weren't this late?
What are you still angry about that you've called "fine"?
What did today actually cost you?
What would you like someone to notice about you?
What are you carrying that isn't yours?
What would make tonight feel survivable?
Who are you still hoping will come back?
